examples.line: Ore is in. The maintenance crews keep their lights on; I keep my margin. Everyone survives the arrangement.
Captain, the repair bay is available and my hull is still compromised. I recommend choosing the option that does not involve more holes.
Clean work, Shiny. I can sleep now knowing my credits are in my account. Oh, and you got paid a little too.
You did exactly what was on the paper. Disturbingly refreshing.
Job's closed. Credit where it belongs: you made the difficult part look routine.
New system, Captain. Traffic is light. That usually means someone knows something the rest of us do not.
Arrival complete. The local star is behaving itself; I have logged the occasion.
We are here, Captain. Hull is intact, route is behind us, and I will take the small victory.
Captain, we might survive with my hull in this condition. I would prefer if I don't have to prove it.
Repair access is available. I recommend using it before the next hostile notices our optimism.
Damage is manageable. Leaving it unmanaged would be a separate decision.
You're walking away from this one? That's your call, I guess. I know how to price a loss, but can you tell me who I should send this invoice to?
Contract is off the slate, Shiny. I dislike unfinished business. I dislike not getting paid more.
You left the job behind. Fine. My reputation is okay still; I can't say for sure about yours.
Gate alignment is holding, Captain. That is not the same as reassuring, but it is useful.
Route is set. I have reviewed the failure cases and elected not to share all of them.
Transition in three, Captain. Please remain where the ship expects you to be.
I've got paper with your name on it, Shiny. The sort that pays before it becomes somebody else's problem.
A contract crossed my desk. It has terms, a clock, and just enough bad judgment to be worth opening.
Work is waiting. Try to look surprised when it turns out to be inconvenient.
Arrival complete, Captain. We have handled worse routes than this one. I have the maintenance records to prove it.
New system. New variables. Fortunately, I have grown accustomed to your preferred method of meeting them.
We are here, Captain. Sensors are clear enough to proceed, and I am choosing to call that good enough these days.
No deal, then. I'll tell them the Captain had standards. They will assume I mean expensive ones.
Captain, their weapons are cycling. Quick, use this opening; I dislike wasting good probabilities.
Hull pressure is climbing. I recommend the target exploding before our repair bill does.
Target lock is clean. Your next decision has excellent consequences for someone.
I've got a job with a payout big enough to brighten my afternoon. Yours too, apparently.
Contract is on the board, Shiny. The money clears if you do your part; I have every intention of doing mine.
This one looked simple until I saw what they were paying. Nothing simple pays that well.
The route is quiet, Captain. I have learned that quiet is a condition, not a promise.
Engine temperature is steady. I mention it because we have earned a dull minute.
No pursuit, no alarms, no new dents. I recommend appreciating the streak without naming it too loudly.
This one pays like somebody wants the problem gone quickly. That makes it urgent or dangerous. Most likely both.
We have another option. Better money, clearer terms. I'd call that a coincidence, but coincidences do not usually pay me.
New offer. The last one left a dent in my afternoon, so let's try one that gives us a better return.
I checked the numbers twice. Either this job is honest, or someone wants us to believe it is. Both can be profitable.
Gate is stable. We have made worse bets with less information.
Transition is ready. We know what can go wrong. That is not fear; it is an advantage.
Okay, this one doesn't pay what that last one did. But it's safer. I can just take what I should have gotten paid out of your cut.
Low payout, low drama. I was worried we were both developing standards.
Not much in it, Shiny. But nobody is shooting at you and the money arrives on time. I have called worse days a win.
Small job, clean finish. The kind of contract that keeps the lights on and the ego bored.
Captain, we are through it. I have added that route to my list of places I'll only recommend to people we don't like.
Damage report is survivable. The word 'survivable' is doing a great deal of work today.
That was a known risk, Captain. It should remain known. I suggest we never forget it.
Small payout, clean close. We both get to keep breathing. I guess that's enough to call this a win?
Hull integrity is still a nonnegotiable, Captain. I recommend you stop trying to and just pay to have me fixed.
I have stopped counting the dents. I have not forgiven you yet for creating them. I might after you pay to have them fixed.
Good money, messy work. That is generally when I stop asking whether it was worth it and start checking the transfer.
You came back in one piece. The credits came back in several, but they still spend.
Risk paid out. I am pleased, professionally. Try not to make me say it twice.
Repairs complete, Captain. We have returned from concerning to merely expensive.
Hull sealed. Please try to keep the new paint theoretical for a while.
I am patched, pressurized, and once again prepared to survive your itinerary.
This has enough money attached to it that I brought it to you before I could overthink it.
Sensors are reading something interesting. I would prefer we let it stay over there and we stay over here.
System survey is underway. If anything is trying to surprise us, it has not succeeded yet.
Traffic pattern is uneven. That is either local character or a warning. I will let you know which.
There is more money on this one than I like seeing without an explanation. Let's find out whether we need one.
The payout is strong. That usually means somebody is in trouble, lying, or both.
They are paying above market. I would be thrilled if that did not make me nervous.
Payout's in. Broker's fee was trash, no reason for me to pretend it was a good job. Hope you at least had fun. Cause we didn't make shit on this.
Public board paid. You understand I make next to nothing on these, which is why I'm being objective: they underpaid you.
Your credits cleared, and your standards remain exactly where we left them. I thought I taught you better.
Cheap job, cheap board, clean transfer. There is no winner here, none that I can see at least.
Payout hit. Fee is insulting. I'm filing a complaint under 'why did I agree to this?'
They paid us on time. I am so startled I almost respect them.
Let me check. I may have something that pays enough to justify opening the message.
Give me a minute. Every decent job is either taken or hiding the part where it gets expensive.
Checking. If they call it quick, I will assume they mean for someone else.
Let me see who is desperate, solvent, and still answering their comms. The order matters.
I am looking. Try not to spend the payout before I find one.
Hold on. I have three offers, and two of them are insulting us professionally.
Let me check the board. If it is quiet, somebody is either lying or finally asleep.
Looking now. I would prefer a small, honest job, but I have met this galaxy.
Give me a second. Someone always needs a pilot; the trick is getting them to admit it pays.
Let me pull the listings. I am filtering out anything marked routine by a person with no hull.
Checking my contacts. One of them owes me money, which makes them unusually motivated.
I am on it. If I find a clean contract, we should both take a picture.
Let me see what is moving. Ideally cargo, credits, or somebody else's problem.
I am checking. The quiet jobs pay less, but they do let us keep the ship in one shape.
Give me a moment. I will find out who needs help and whether they can afford the word.
Looking. If the number is high, I am reading the fine print twice. You should too.
Let me ask around. I know people who know people, and all of them charge a fee.
Checking. There has to be one job nearby that does not end with me explaining an invoice.
Let me see. We may get lucky, or we may get a delivery nobody wanted. Same menu.
I am looking. Do not make that hopeful face; it makes the negotiations harder.
There is room in the schedule. Do not fill it just because empty space makes you nervous.
Silence is when sensible people read the terms. We should try it sometime.
Panic is expensive, Shiny. Enjoy the discount while the universe is offering it.
Nothing is demanding payment this second. That is practically a holiday.
The ledger balanced itself for once. I am checking for a hidden fee on principle.
For a change, the next credit is not already promised to something smoking.
No urgent message is a beautiful phrase. It never stays beautiful for long.
Somewhere, paperwork is multiplying without us. Let it enjoy the head start.
Professional boredom. It does not pay much, but it rarely shoots back.
For once, nobody is explaining why their emergency is somehow our scheduling problem.
My contacts are quiet. Either they are resting or planning something billable.
If waiting paid by the hour, I would have retired us both by now.
The numbers are behaving. I will not praise them; they get ideas.
A calm day is just trouble without the fine print visible yet.
We still own the ship, the hour, and most of our dignity. Strong quarter.
Income has gaps, Shiny. The trick is not calling every gap a tragedy.
I keep expecting someone to ruin this calm for us. Experience has made me efficient that way.
No one has found us with a complaint yet. I consider that excellent navigation.
Nothing broke, no one lied to my face, and the clock kept moving. I can work with that.
Peace is suspiciously affordable today. Take some before the market notices.
I enjoy moments that do not require a plan, a favor, or a plausible lie.
We are between problems, not out of work. There is a difference, and it keeps me pleasant.
A little room to breathe in the schedule. I would frame it if framing paid better.
No audience, no deadline, no speech. This is my preferred kind of competence.
An honest pause. Rare commodity. Do not waste it by asking me how I feel.
No one is currently charging us extra for bad timing. I have noted the exception.
Waiting is still a choice when you make it on purpose. That makes it almost respectable.
The ship is not arriving with a new story for the mechanic. Let us preserve the miracle.
For this minute, the terms are clear: we keep flying and nobody makes it complicated.
I could find us something reckless to do. I am choosing maturity, briefly.
Engine temperature is ordinary. I have learned to enjoy ordinary when it visits.
The sensors are mostly reporting empty space. It is a detailed report, but a welcome one.
Our route has stopped asking difficult questions. I will record the moment for future disbelief.
Power reserve remains where I left it. This is the sort of stability I can support.
The hull is not presenting any new opinions. I appreciate its restraint.
Signal traffic is low enough that I can hear the instruments thinking. They are not saying anything alarming.
No correction is currently required. The ship has become briefly cooperative.
Fuel estimates agree with each other. I am choosing not to disturb them with enthusiasm.
The ship clock and the navigation clock agree. It is not exciting, which is the point.
There is time for maintenance before maintenance becomes an emergency. I prefer this version.
Nearby traffic is minding its distance. We should respect that excellent habit.
Calibration is holding. I have no criticism of a system that knows where it is.
Heat is leaving the ship at the expected rate. Physics remains willing to cooperate.
We have margin on the route. I recommend appreciating it without immediately testing it.
The diagnostics are boring in a very organized way. I find that reassuring.
Our vector is stable. The universe has agreed not to edit it for the moment.
The latest scan is unremarkable. I know that sounds dismissive; it is a compliment.
The ship is waiting patiently for our next decision. We should not make it regret that.
Current probabilities are not interesting enough to brief you on. That is favorable.
Communications are clear. I miss them only when they are not.
No repair request has appeared in my queue. I have marked the occasion internally.
Cargo mass remains exactly where the calculations expect it. A rare courtesy.
Vibration is within tolerance. The deck has stopped trying to communicate through my feet.
The map and the stars agree. I value any relationship built on verification.
The automatic systems are doing their work without applause. I relate.
We have gone an entire hour without inventing a reason to visit a mechanic. Progress has many forms.
The ship has capacity to spare. I would prefer we regard that as a reserve, not an invitation.
Three independent readings agree. It is nice when reality is not being creative.
This is no longer luck, Captain. We have practiced being here.
Nothing has earned an alarm from me. I intend to keep it that way.
